analysis: Examined two changes. (1) NativeServeQualification.swift line 32-33: adds DARKBLOOM_VERIFIED_WEIGHTS_FILE redirected into the 0700 private state directory (mkdir 0o700 at line 29, umask 077 at line 17). This reduces the chance the opt-in diagnostic touches operator-global verified-weights state. It is a narrowing change, with no new attacker-controlled input; the path derives from inputs.directory validated by NativeServeQualificationInputs (not shown). The consumer of the env var is outside the supplied evidence, so I assume it honors the override. No finding. (2) EngineV2Bridge+Submission.swift: adds an early refusal (head ~149-153, helper ~960-990) for native-tracked engines when the request has token constraints or logprobs the engine cannot capture. It throws the typed unsupportedOutputControl error before any service allowance, KV reservation, pendingSubmissionIDs insertion or prefix staging, so there is no resource to unwind. The refusal calls usageSignal?.finalizeLookup(failure: .policy) and continuation.finish(), matching the existing early-rejection pattern. The nonthrowing overload now catches unsupportedOutputControl and yields the content-free message in-band. The message is a fixed prefix plus a static string and includes no prompt content, so it does not leak A-001. The early guard sits before duplicate-ID checks and before the calibration await. It does not alter cache-scope handling (T-041) or authorization. It is a fail-closed change that avoids misattributed generation failures striking the coordinator inference-error breaker. Remaining integration questions, which cannot be verified here: that MultiModelBatchSchedulerEngineError.unsupportedOutputControl and EngineV2Translation.unsupportedOutputControlPrefix exist and map to a client 4xx in callers (fromSchedulerMessage), and that engine?.acceptsLogprobRows defaults to true (capture) for non-EngineV2 owners, so the refusal applies only when nativeTracked. No security regression identified.
